description: 1997 is the Year of the Fire Ox in the Chinese zodiac, from February 7, 1997 to January 27, 1998. Personality, Lunar New Year dates and numerology.
answer: In Chinese astrology, 1997 is the Year of the Fire Ox, a Yin year. It began at Lunar New Year on February 7, 1997 and ended on January 27, 1998, so people born in 1997 before Feb 7 belong to the Fire Rat year.

sections.heading: 1997 Lunar New Year: start and end dates
paragraphs: Lunar New Year opened the Fire Ox year on February 7, 1997, and the year ran to January 27, 1998. So a birth date of Feb 7, 1997 or later counts as Fire Ox, and so do early 1998 birthdays through Jan 27; births in 1997 before Feb 7 still belong to the Fire Rat. That moving boundary comes from the lunisolar calendar, in which the new year starts with the second new moon after the winter solstice in most years, so its Gregorian date shifts by up to a month from one year to the next. Look sixty years either side and the pairing repeats: 1937 are Fire Ox years too. That Friday new year arrived with the Sun in Aquarius in the Western zodiac.

sections.heading: What the Fire Ox is like
paragraphs: People born in a Fire Ox year are often pictured as tireless leaders with strong convictions. Fire generating Earth is read as warmth fuelling endurance, so this Ox has unusual drive. They tend to defend their views energetically. Readings suggest asking for input before deciding, accepting that others move at different speeds and building regular rest into a busy, purposeful life.

Belonging to the south and to the height of summer, Fire brings brightness, drive and visibility to any sign it colours. Classical texts connect it with enthusiasm, leadership and the urge to be seen and to make an impression. A Fire stem tends to make an animal more expressive, more daring and more openly emotional than its usual reputation suggests. People born in Fire years are often described as inspiring company and natural motivators. The caution most readings attach is a short fuse and a difficulty with slow seasons, when steady effort matters more than spark and the reward is a long way off.

sections.heading: 1997 in the animal cycle and in numerology
paragraphs: In numerology the digits reduce to 8, associated with ambition, authority and material results, so an 8 year is described in terms of effort and reward. The digits of 1997 add up to 26, which reduces to 8. The Ox holds the second place among the twelve animals and its fixed element is Earth. Set beside the year's Fire stem, fire generates Earth, which readings use to describe how settled or stretched the combination feels. The year before was the Fire Rat and the year after is the Earth Tiger.

Chinese almanacs name 1997 Ding-Chou, pairing the Fire stem Ding with the branch Chou. Both are Yin, as stem and branch always share a polarity, so of the hundred and twenty possible pairings only sixty ever occur, and each one names a single year in every cycle.

faq.question: What Chinese zodiac is 1997?
faq.answer: 1997 is the Year of the Fire Ox. It started on February 7, 1997 and ended on January 27, 1998.

faq.question: What if I was born in January or February 1997?
faq.answer: Check the date against Feb 7. Born before February 7, 1997, you are a Fire Rat; born on or after it, you are a Fire Ox.

faq.question: What element is 1997 in the Chinese zodiac?
faq.answer: Fire, a Yin year. The Ox's own fixed element is Earth; the year element changes every two years, while the fixed element stays with the animal.

faq.question: What is the traditional Chinese name for 1997?
faq.answer: Ding-Chou. The first part is the heavenly stem, which carries the year's element and polarity; the second is the earthly branch, which carries the animal. Almanacs, calendars and Four Pillars charts identify years this way rather than by animal alone.

faq.question: When is the next Fire Ox year?
faq.answer: 2057, sixty years later, when the five elements and twelve animals line up again; the table also has 1937.
